newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paribas ends bank stock roll on high.
newsitem.headline: Paribas ends bank stock roll on high.

text.p: Groupe Paribas ended a rip-roaring week for long-languishing French bank stocks 12 percent higher after a huge merger plan between insurer Axa and UAP prompted a wave of merger and acquisition speculation.

Paribas hit a year high of 369.0 francs before shedding just 30 centimes to 368.7 francs at the close on Friday, 5.04 percent up on the day and 12 percent above the closing level of 329.0 last Friday.

The stock market ended on a new high too, in a bullish week which opened on Tuesday after a holiday weekend, with the news from Axa and UAP that they had agreed to merge and create the world's second largest insurer.

Paribas starred, with analysts citing revived speculation on bank stocks in the belief that the sheer scale of the Axa merger had transformed the complex cross-shareholding relationships of power in French banking and made the idea of further mergers and acquisitions more tenable.

Paribas chairman Andre Levy-Lang also said in an interview in Le Journal des Finances that it would eventually part with its Via Banque unit, which was the biggest gainer of the day, up 18.43 percent on Friday at 158.7 francs.

Banque Nationale de Paris, which surged 8.5 percent the day of the Axa/UAP announcement from a close of 119.9 francs last Friday to end the week 5.7 percent higher at 211.4, with a poor performance on Friday attributed to profit-taking.

Traders and newspapers have revived many long-running merger and acquisition scenarios with added gusto in the wake of the Axa/UAP pact, with the idea that Paribas's investment bank unit Banque Paribas would have to link up with a French retail bank to create a less volatile source of revenue.
BNP was highlighted as an option but analysts said it was impossible amid the renewed excitement to read too much into the various scenarios.

The investment community is still getting to grips with the implications of the Axa/UAP deal, which will create the biggest group on the Paris bourse, with the highest level of assets under management in the world.

But one highlighted that it would hold almost 11 percent in each of Paribas and BNP and as a new heavyweight would start looking for a far bigger say in their management and shareholder value from the two major French banks.
The other big quoted French bank, Societe Generale, ended the week 2.8 percent higher at 577 francs.
Axa, which is seen as the big brother and the boss in the merger with UAP, ended the week 5.3 percent lower at 301.6 francs, from 318.5 francs at last Friday's close.
UAP ended 14.7 percent higher at 134.1 francs from a close last Friday of 116.9 francs.

Compagnie de Suez, which earlier this year sold control of its Banque Indosuez to Credit Agricole in the biggest event for French financials prior to the Axa/UAP deal, also gained ground on Friday, up 1.86 percent at 224.1 francs.

But that move was partly attributed to a newspaper report that it was close to selling off its 4.4 billion franc property portfolio. Traders said a loss of 2.0 to 2.5 billion francs on this sale had been factored into the share price already and that the share rose on the idea of it getting rid of its woes in a moribund French property sector.
